newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - ACPC agrees export cuts to support robustas.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ACPC agrees export cuts to support robustas.

text.p: Members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) agreed to slice exports further in the first half of 1997 in a show of support for robusta producers, concerned by a wide difference between arabica and robusta prices.

The decision to cut an additional 1.3 million 60-kg bags was taken at an extraordinary council meeting in Rio de Janeiro, called after African producers said there was a need for exports in January to June to be reduced by 2.5 million bags.

African producers were very encouraged by the outcome of the meeting, saying that the lower total was in line with a rise in arabica and more recently robusta prices which had taken place since the proposal was originally made public in December.

"We are very pleased...Things have changed in terms of production forecasts, in terms of world stocks. We took all these into consideration and decided on a smaller reduction," said the Ivorian Minister for Commodities, Guy-Alain Gauze.
The cut will be divided out into one million bags by robusta producers and 300,000 bags by arabica producers and it is now up to both groups to sort out individual countries' contributions.
This will be done in the case of robusta producers at a special meeting to be held in Bali on February 6, Gauze said.
Discussions amongst arabica producers will be conducted by telephone over the next week, said the head of the primary commodities department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry.
Of extreme political importance is a commitment by major robusta producer Indonesia to take part in the reductions,
"We will make our contribution, we will take part," said Derek Watson, adviser to the Indonesian delegation, after the meeting.

Indonesia had previously shown some reluctance to join any further effort to limit exports due to fears rival producer Vietnam, a non-ACPC member, would take advantage of the situation to win more market share.
Under a plan agreed by the ACPC in May last year, exports in the first half of 1997 should not have exceeded 26.28 million bags.
This was to follow exports of 27.27 million bags in July to December but which in reality reached 28.13 million bags, according to ACPC officials today.
There was no reason to be concerned by the small excess, especially given the continued fall in consumer stocks, said the ACPC secretary-general Roberio Oliveira da Silva.
"There was an small overshoot, yes," da Silva said.

"But before we started the export program, we had been told consumer stocks were 8.9 million bags. The idea of the program was to maintain stocks at eight million bags but now we are being told they are 7.5 million bags. So even with the slightly higher exports, they have still fallen more than we expected," he added.
